targets.title: The role of feasibility and desirability considerations in near and distant future decisions: A test of temporal construal theory
targets.evidence_quote:
Using an international multilab approach, we
directly replicated the following two studies: Liberman
and Trope (1998, Study 1; temporal distance) and Fujita
et al. (2006, Study 1; spatial distance).
targets.outcome_quote:
According to our preregistered criteria, the replication effect for temporal distance was consistent in
direction but inconsistent in magnitude with the original
effect reported by Liberman and Trope (1998, Study 1):
The main analysis revealed an effect in the predicted
direction with a CI that excluded zero, but the observed
effect (d = 0.08, 95% CI = [0.003, 0.16]) was only 9% the
size of the original effect (d = 0.92), and the upper bound
of the replication CI excluded the original effect size.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly report an effect in the predicted direction. The much smaller magnitude alone does not make this mixed; the overall limited-support statement concerns the four theoretical tests collectively.

targets.authors: Fujita, K., Henderson, M. D., Eng, J., Trope, Y., & Liberman, N.
targets.title: Spatial distance and mental construal of social events
targets.evidence_quote:
Using an international multilab approach, we
directly replicated the following two studies: Liberman
and Trope (1998, Study 1; temporal distance) and Fujita
et al. (2006, Study 1; spatial distance).
targets.outcome_quote:
The replication effects for
spatial distance and likelihood were small and had CIs
that included zero, failing to support the original predictions.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors state the spatial-distance replication failed to support the original prediction.

reasoning: Completed new-sample direct replications of two original papers. Social distance and likelihood are paradigmatic extensions: authors explain that no suitable originals were identified for these distances and they substituted manipulations in the basic paradigms. No additional specific original finding is identified as their target. No numerical replication-study labels are assigned in the paper.
